title: Preoperative and Postoperative Radiosurgery in Patients With Brain Metastases Undergoing Surgery
official: Randomized Phase II/III Study Comparing Preoperative Radiosurgery Versus Postoperative Radiosurgery in Patients With Brain Metastases Eligible for Surgery: Correlation With Histopathological Factors and Radiomic Analysis.
summary:
The PREOP-RAD study aims to evaluate the feasibility, safety, and efficacy of preoperative surgical resection (SRS) in patients with large brain metastases requiring surgical resection, taking into account potential differences based on sex/gender, compared to postoperative SRS, within the Spanish healthcare context.

More specifically, the study seeks to:

* Assess the clinical and radiological outcomes of the preoperative strategy in terms of local control, progression-free survival, and the occurrence of radionecrosis or neuromuscular dysfunction (nMD) compared to the postoperative strategy.
* Study the histopathological profile of resected lesions before and after SRS, searching for personalized biomarkers of response and toxicity.
* Identify patterns based on radiomic analysis and advanced imaging related to therapeutic response, recurrence, and complications.

PREOP-RAD is a prospective, randomized, multicenter study that will include patients diagnosed with symptomatic, single or multiple brain metastases ≥2 cm who are candidates for surgical resection. The procedure will consist of preoperative administration of SRS (1-5 fractions, depending on location and size), followed by surgery within a maximum of 10 days.

The intervention will be carried out in coordination with the Neurosurgery and Radiation Oncology Departments of each participating center, using a standardized workflow. The collection of surgical samples will allow for centralized histopathological studies. Furthermore, pre- and postoperative images will undergo radiomic analysis using artificial intelligence tools to explore similarities and correlate morphological and textural characteristics with clinical outcomes.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age ≥18 years.
* Histologically confirmed solid tumor with one to four brain metastases.
* At least one brain metastasis considered suitable for surgical resection and stereotactic radiosurgery.
* Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) ≥70.
* Life expectancy ≥3 months.
* Ability to undergo MRI examinations.
* Written informed consent provided.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Brain metastases from small-cell lung cancer, germ cell tumors, lymphoma, or leukemia.
* Prior radiotherapy to the index lesion.
* Leptomeningeal disease at baseline.
* Contraindication to surgery or stereotactic radiosurgery.
* Pregnancy or breastfeeding.
* Any condition that, in the investigator's opinion, would interfere with study participation or evaluation.
